extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, and registered practitioners (U.S. patent attorneys/agents) and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on calculating, determining, reducing, and seeking reconsideration of patent term adjustment (PTA) under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and implementing regulations (37 CFR 1.703–1.705), including what applicant actions constitute failures to engage in reasonable efforts. Focused on U.S. practice before the USPTO (MPEP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of PTA for late compliant appeal brief after a non‑compliant brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant files a non-compliant appeal brief and thereafter files a compliant appeal brief, the period from filing the non-compliant brief to filing the compliant brief will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination under 37 CFR 1.704(c)(8). However, if the compliant appeal brief is filed more than three months from the date the notice of appeal was filed, the provisions of 37 CFR 1.704(c)(11) may result in reduction of any patent term adjustment under 37 CFR 1.703.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key timing rule: compliant appeal brief filed within three months of the notice of appeal avoids being treated as applicant delay for PTA; filing after three months may trigger PTA reduction under 1.704(c)(11).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(11) counting rule for appeal delays
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(11) provides that the period of adjustment set forth in 37 CFR 1.703 shall be reduced by the number of days, if any, beginning on the day after the date three months from the date on which the notice of appeal to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board was filed and ending on the date an appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37 or a request for continued examination in compliance with 37 CFR 1.114 was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate reduction days from (three months after notice of appeal + 1 day) until filing of a compliant brief or an RCE in compliance with 1.114. This is the formal statutory/regulatory measure for appeal-related applicant delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of USPTO reopening prosecution before compliant appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office reopens prosecution of the application more than three months after filing the notice of appeal but prior to submission of a compliant appeal brief, the Office will not deem the period from the day after three months to the date the Office reopens prosecution to be an applicant delay under 37 CFR 1.704(c)(11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO-initiated reopening during this window negates applicant-delay counting under 1.704(c)(11). Reopening also will not be considered vacating any prior response that potentially increased PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after notice of allowance constitutes applicant failure (37 CFR 1.704(c)(12))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a request for continued examination (RCE) under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) after any notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 is treated as a failure of an applicant to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination, and the period of adjustment under 37 CFR 1.703 shall be reduced by the number of days beginning on the day after the date of mailing of the notice of allowance and ending on the date the RCE was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents applicants from gaining PTA by filing an RCE after a notice of allowance (i.e., delaying issuance). The filing of such an RCE removes the application from the issue process and will generally reduce PTA for the period between allowance mailing and RCE filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for RCE-after-allowance PTA reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an RCE after mailing of a notice of allowance removes the application from the issue process, prevents the Office from issuing the patent, and requires the Office to determine if the submission affects the patentability of the application, thereby adding to pendency and diverting examination resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the applicant’s action prolongs pendency and burdens Office resources, the Office treats it as a failure to engage in reasonable efforts for purposes of PTA calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS submission within thirty days avoids PTA reduction (37 CFR 1.704(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office permits applicants to submit information cited in a patent office communication in a counterpart application to the Office without a reduction in PTA if an information disclosure statement (IDS) is submitted to the Office within thirty days (not three months) of the date the patent office communication was received by an individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely IDS (within 30 days from receipt by a designated person) plus required statements will avoid reductions under specified 1.704(c) paragraphs. The 30-day window is strict and not extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE accompanied only by IDS not a failure if 1.704(d) statement present
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.704(d) was revised to provide that a request for continued examination in compliance with 37 CFR 1.114 with no submission other than an IDS in compliance with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution under 37 CFR 1.704(c)(12), if the RCE is accompanied by a statement in compliance with 37 CFR 1.704(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid PTA reduction when filing an RCE with only an IDS, include the specific 1.704(d) statement. The IDS itself must comply with 1.97/1.98.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content/statement requirements of 37 CFR 1.704(d)(1)(i) and (ii)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.704(d) requires that each item of information in the IDS be accompanied by a statement that (i) it was first cited in any communication from a patent office in a counterpart foreign or international application or from the Office, and that this communication was not received by any individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) more than thirty days prior to the filing of the IDS; or (ii) it is a communication issued by a patent office in a counterpart foreign or international application or by the Office, and this communication was not received by any individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) more than thirty days prior to the filing of the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and include the precise statement called for by 1.704(d) to qualify for the 30-day safe harbor. Compliance with 1.704(d) does not substitute for compliance with 1.97/1.98, and the 30-day period is non-extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of individuals designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.56(c) provides that individuals associated with the filing or prosecution of a patent application include: (1) each inventor named in the application; (2) each attorney or agent who prepares or prosecutes the application; and (3) every other person who is substantively involved in the preparation or prosecution of the application and who is associated with the inventor, the assignee or with anyone to whom there is an obligation to assign the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether foreign counsel or others are 'designated' persons depends on their substantive role in U.S. prosecution; three illustrative examples (A, B, C) clarify how to apply 1.56(c) for the 30-day IDS safe harbor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example-based guidance on when the 30‑day IDS period begins
rubrics_metrics.description: Three examples illustrate start dates for the 30-day period under 1.704(d): Example A (foreign counsel with no substantive role) — 30-day period counted from U.S. counsel receipt; Example B (foreign counsel substantively involved in drafting/prosecution) — 30-day period counted from foreign counsel receipt; Example C (foreign counsel substantively involved in prosecution decisions) — 30-day period counted from the date foreign counsel learned of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the examples to determine whether foreign counsel are 'designated' persons under 1.56(c) and thus when the 30-day clock runs. Substantive participation in U.S. drafting/prosecution points to counting from their receipt date.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(e) reinstatement requests not applicant failure
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.704(e) provides that a submission of a request under 37 CFR 1.705(c) for reinstatement of reduced patent term adjustment will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution (processing or examination) of the application under 37 CFR 1.704(c)(10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because statute requires such requests be filed prior to issuance, filing a reinstatement request itself is not charged as applicant delay for PTA purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to provide application in condition for examination within eight months (37 CFR 1.704(c)(13))
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after December 18, 2013 (and certain international national-stage filings), failure to provide an application in condition for examination within eight months from filing or commencement of national stage constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts, and the period of adjustment under 1.703 shall be reduced by the number of days beginning on the day after that eight‑month date and ending on the date the application is in condition for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The eight-month window is measured from the filing date (or national-stage commencement). An application need not be in condition on filing to avoid reduction, but if not placed in condition within eight months PTA will be reduced accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing applications constitute failure to engage in reasonable efforts (37 CFR 1.704(c)(14))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(14) establishes that further prosecution via a continuing application (continuation, divisional, continuation-in-part) is a circumstance that constitutes a failure of an applicant to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination of an application; PTA for the patent will not include any period prior to the actual filing date of the application that resulted in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA does not carry over from prior/parent filings into a continuing application; periods prior to the actual filing date of the application that resulted in the patent are excluded from the PTA calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA (continued prosecution application) PTA limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d) filed within specified date windows may be entitled to PTA, but the period of PTA will not include any period prior to the filing date of the request for that CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where CPAs are eligible for PTA, the PTA period is measured only from the CPA request filing date (or applicable CPA filing date) and does not include earlier periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delays in prior applications not relevant to PTA for current patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Delays before the filing date of an application are not relevant to whether an application is entitled to PTA. PTA will not be reduced by applicant actions or inactions occurring in a prior (or other) application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only events in the application that resulted in the patent (or governed by the cited regulatory provisions) are relevant for PTA; prior-application delays do not reduce PTA for the later-filed patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'condition for examination' per 37 CFR 1.704(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is in condition for examination when it includes: a specification including at least one claim and an abstract (37 CFR 1.72(b)); papers in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52; drawings in compliance with 37 CFR 1.84; any required English translation (37 CFR 1.52(d) or 1.57(a)); a sequence listing in compliance with 37 CFR 1.821–1.825 (if applicable); the inventor's oath or declaration or application data sheet with information specified in 37 CFR 1.63(b); the basic filing fee (1.16(a)/(c)); the search fee (1.16(k)/(m)); the examination fee (1.16(o)/(q)); any certified copy required by 1.57(a); and any application size fee required under 1.16(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International applications entering the national stage have parallel requirements (e.g., 1.492 series fees). Papers/drawings/sequence listings corrected by a reply before the first action or notice of allowance are considered compliant as of the filing date of the latest correcting reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rule for corrected papers/drawings/sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.704(f) provides that an application shall be considered as having papers in compliance with 1.52, drawings in compliance with 1.84, and sequence listings in compliance with 1.821–1.825 on the filing date of the latest reply (if any) correcting the papers, drawings, or sequence listing that is prior to the date of mailing of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections timely made before the first action or notice of allowance are effective as of the filing date of the correction for condition-for-examination purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTA notice on patent; AIA Technical Corrections timing (37 CFR 1.705)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent will include notification of any patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b). The AIA Technical Corrections Act amended 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(3)(B)(i) so the Office shall transmit a determination of the PTA no later than the date of issuance of the patent; the Office will continue to provide a preliminary PTA calculation with the issue notification but the PTA indicated on the patent is the 'official' determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should rely on the PTA printed on the issued patent as the official determination; preliminary figures with the issue notification are not final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for disclosing alleged Office error when PTA indicated is greater
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registered practitioner receives a PTA indicated on the front of the patent that is longer than expected, the practitioner may disclose the error to the Office in a letter in compliance with the practitioner's duty of candor and good faith. The Office will place such letters in the file of the patent without comment and will not review these letters or issue certificates of correction on that basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters alleging the Office's PTA is greater are treated as file comments; they do not trigger Office review or correction unless pursued via the formal reconsideration procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates of correction will not revise PTA except in limited circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not grant a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 254 or 255 to revise the PTA indicated in a patent unless the certificate of correction is issued to revise the patent for consistency with (1) the PTA determined via a decision on the request for reconsideration under 37 CFR 1.705, or (2) the total PTA indicated on the PAIR screen that displays the PTA calculation for the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patentee submits a certificate of correction that attempts to revise PTA along with other patent corrections, the request will not be granted unless a new request is submitted that does not attempt to revise PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 37 CFR 1.705(b) reconsideration procedures for PTA disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patentee wants the Office to reconsider its PTA determination, the patentee must use procedures set forth in 37 CFR 1.705(b) for requesting reconsideration of a patent term adjustment determination. These procedures must be used whether the Office's PTA is greater than or less than what the applicant believes is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the formal 1.705(b) process (timing, fee, required statement contents) rather than informal letters when seeking PTA reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer as remedy for excess PTA
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may file a terminal disclaimer at any time disclaiming any period considered in excess of the appropriate PTA. See 35 U.S.C. 253 and 37 CFR 1.321.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a terminal disclaimer is an available option to remove excess PTA; it is not required when PTA on the patent is greater than believed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAI R review and checking Office receipt dates for PTA accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Information as to how the PTA calculation has been made will be available through PAIR. Applicants may routinely use PAIR to check the accuracy of data entered in the PALM system (type of paper and date of receipt). The date recorded should be the date of receipt, not the date mailed under 37 CFR 1.8. If an original paper is misplaced and a duplicate is filed with a postcard receipt showing the date of receipt of the original paper, that date should be shown in Office records. If Priority Mail Express was used, the 'date accepted' on the label will be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor PAIR/PALM throughout prosecution and promptly notify the examiner or Technology Center customer service of errors so they can be corrected before allowance and final PTA determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.705(b) filing requirements and timing for PTA reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reconsideration of the PTA indicated on the patent must be by way of an application for PTA filed no later than two months from the date the patent was granted (extendable under 1.136(a)). The application must be accompanied by (1) the fee set forth in 1.18(e); and (2) a statement specifying: (i) the correct PTA and the basis or bases under 1.702 for the adjustment; (ii) the relevant dates as specified in 1.703(a)–(e) for which an adjustment is sought and the adjustment as specified in 1.703(f) to which the patent is entitled; (iii) whether the patent is subject to a terminal disclaimer and any expiration date specified therein; and (iv)(A) any circumstances during prosecution that constitute a failure under 1.704, or (B) that there were no circumstances constituting such a failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict two-month deadline (subject to extension rules) and specific contents/fee are required for a valid PTA reconsideration application under 1.705(b). Provide full factual and regulatory basis referencing 1.702–1.704 and 1.703 date calculations.
